text:
james: Ran overnight profiler after the kernel-selector tweak — p95 decode latency up ~18% on short-turn chat traces. Traces point at cross-phase batching interference when prefill + decode share queue. KV cache drain spikes line up with decode insert storms.

tara: link to traces? :eyes:

james: perf-bot uploaded the perf bundle: https://perf.internal/redwood/1768901234 — see trace flame, KV evictions around decode flushes.

kevin: my hunch: prefill forms large mixed batches that delay small decode batches. Separate queues + phase-aware priorities should help (and give us per-phase token budgets).

sri: also watch KV hotspotting. If prefill churns KV entries, decode misses will amplify tail. Might need a small "KV reserve" for decode flows so they don't get completely cold.

james: proposal sketch: split queues (prefill, decode), give decode higher priority + smaller token_budget target so it ships quickly. Let prefill batch larger when queue is long to amortize kernel launch. Add backoff if KV eviction rate > threshold.

kevin: concrete defaults I tried locally (toy harness):
```
queues:
  - name: prefill
    priority: 1
    token_budget: 1024
    batch_target_ms: 20
  - name: decode
    priority: 2
    token_budget: 256
    batch_target_ms: 5
kv:
  reserve_for_decode: true
  reserve_tokens: 64
```
These cut p95 decode by ~12% on short-turn runs, p50 unchanged, small cost win due to less KV churn.

tara: nice. how will we test/measure in prod?

james: A/B rollout plan: start 5% traffic with new scheduler, monitor p50/p95 for both prefill and decode, kv_miss_rate, kv_eviction_count, token_budget_utilization, kernel-selection changes. 48h observation window, auto-rollback on >10% p95 regression.

perf-bot: Uploaded dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/sched-experiments/176890 — p95 latency, kv_evictions, queue_sizes.

sri: small note on kernel selection: decode batches are short sequences, prefer low-latency kernels (fast-keops or fused-attn) — ensure scheduler hints kernel chooser with phase meta (prefill vs decode) and seq_len histograms.

kevin: add backpressure rule: if kv_eviction_rate > 0.3 then increase prefill.batch_target_ms => bigger prefill batches, fewer evictions. Also cap prefill concurrency to avoid thrash.

james: I'll open PR with scheduling config + observability metrics (queue_size, token_budget_util_pct, kv_eviction_count, kernel_selected). Assigning @tara to own experiment dashboard and alerts.

tara: ack. timeline?

james: PR by EOD, perf job tomorrow morning, start canary 5% by tomorrow afternoon, evaluate 48h.

kevin: logging points to add in PR: `scheduler.queue_len`, `scheduler.batch_formed_tokens`, `scheduler.token_budget_used`, `kv.evictions`, `kernel.selection_reason` — these are cheap and will help root-cause fast.

james: will include those. Also adding a tiny postmortem checklist: if decode p95 regresses on canary, revert queue-split and try token_budget tweak only.

sri: one more: measure tail of KV latency (not just miss rate) — decode is sensitive to a few 100ms KV slowdowns.

perf-bot: Noted — added KV latency chart to the experiment dashboard.

james: great. thanks all. I'll post PR link in this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:
